newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia vows quick NATO entry despite US move.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia vows quick NATO entry despite US move.

text.p: The former Yugoslav republic of Slovenia pledged on Thursday to pursue its bid for quick NATO membership despite a U.S. announcement saying it favoured expansion only for three other ex-communist states.

"Slovenia enjoys the support of at least nine NATO member nations for its candidature," Foreign Minister Zoran Thaler said in a statement issued by the Slovenian news agency STA. "This support is getting stronger and other members are not opposed to our bid."
The statement said Slovenia would pursue its campaign right up until next month's NATO summit in Madrid, where the candidates for enlargement eastward are to be announced.

The U.S. announcement at a NATO meeting in Brussels said President Bill Clinton's administration favoured including only favourites Poland, Hungary and the Czech Republic and leaving out Romania and Slovenia.

Slovenia has received particularly strong backing from Italy, its western neighbour. Some French and German officials have also offered support but it was not clear to which backer countries Thaler was referring.

Romanian officials said they believed the U.S. move failed to take account of Washington's interests in eastern Europe and suggested that the Clinton administration could be persuaded to change its mind by the Madrid summit.
